::: {style="width: 80%; margin: auto;"}
![](images/structured-data.png)
:::

:::{.gray-text .center-text}
*The same data, in two different shapes.*

:::

For five days every question you asked was a question about one table, and you got away with it
because somebody had already put everything you needed in one place.

That is not how data usually arrives. It arrives as two files that describe the same thing from
different angles, or as thirty files that describe different things in the same format, or as one
file laid out at right angles to the question you want to ask. Before you can analyse any of that,
you have to change its shape.

Today you learn the three sentences that do it. One puts two tables **side by side**. One stacks
many tables **top to bottom**. One takes a single table and **rotates** it. None of them calculates
anything, and without them most of what you learned last week cannot be applied to real files.

This afternoon you meet the column that is hardest to get into the right shape, because it usually
does not admit to being a date at all.
